questions.question: The circumference of a circle of diameter 14 cm is the same as the perimeter of a square. The area of the square is (take π = (22)/(7)):
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The circumference of a circle of diameter 14 cm is the same as the perimeter of a square.

**Formula used:**

Circumference of a circle = 2πr

Area of a square = a²

The perimeter of a square = 4a

Here, r = radius of the circle & a = side of the square

**Calculation:**

The radius of the circle = 14/2 = 7 cm

Let the side of the square be 'a'

Now, 2 × (22/7) × 7 = 4 × a

⇒ 44 = 4a

⇒ a = 11

Now, Area of the square = 11² = 121

**∴ The area of the square is 121 cm2**.

questions.question: Numerically, what percentage of its circumference is the area of a circle of radius 4?

questions.question: The radii of two circles are 20 cm and 15 cm respectively. If a third circle has an area that is equal to the sum of the areas of the two given circles, what will be the radius of the third circle?
questions.solution:

radius (r₁) = 20 cm

radius (r₂) = 15 cm

Area of a circle is (A) = πr²

**Concept used:**

The area of the third circle, A₃ = A₂ + A₁

**Calculation:**

A₁ = π r₁²

⇒ A₁ = π × 20²

⇒ A₁ = 400 × π

A₂ = πr ₂²

⇒ A₂ = π × 15²

⇒ A₂ = 225 × π

A₃ = A₂ + A₁

⇒ A₃ = 400 × π + 225 × π

**∴ The radius of the third circle is 25 cm.**

questions.question: If the diameter of a circle is increased by 24%, then the percentage increase in the area is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

If the diameter of a circle is increased by 24%, then the percentage increase in the area is:

**Formula used:**

Area of a circle = πr²

New diameter = original diameter × (1 + 24/100)

New radius = new diameter / 2

Percentage increase in area = ((New Area - Original Area) / Original Area) × 100%

**Calculation:**

Let the original diameter be D, then the original radius r = D/2

New diameter = D × (1 + 24/100) = D × 1.24

New radius = (D × 1.24) / 2 = 0.62D

Original Area = πr² = π(D/2)² = πD²/4

New Area = π(0.62D)² = π(0.3844D²) = 0.3844πD²

Percentage increase in area = ((New Area - Original Area) / Original Area) × 100%

⇒ Percentage increase in area = ((0.3844πD² - πD²/4) / (πD²/4)) × 100%

⇒ Percentage increase in area = ((0.3844 - 0.25) / 0.25) × 100%

⇒ Percentage increase in area = (0.1344 / 0.25) × 100%

⇒ Percentage increase in area = 53.76%

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question:
A wire is in the form of a square of side 33 cm. If the wire is molded to form a circle, then what is the radius of the circle? 

(Use pi = {22 over 7})
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a wire is remolded, the total length (perimeter) remains constant.

Circumference of Circle = Perimeter of Square

2 × (22 / 7) × r = 4 × 33

(44 / 7) × r = 132 ⇒ r = 3 × 7 = 21 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 21 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the square (a) = 33 cm

π = 22 / 7

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of a square = 4 × a

Circumference of a circle = 2 × π × r (where r is the radius)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b90186e50b7eef4f799c922119a5273b552448e8dedb8f9f7e61429e76863ca4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total length of the wire = Perimeter of the square

⇒ Total length of the wire = 4 × 33 = 132 cm

⇒ When the same wire is bent into a circle, Circumference = Total length of the wire

⇒ 2 × π × r = 132

⇒ 2 × (22 / 7) × r = 132

⇒ (44 / 7) × r = 132

⇒ r = (132 × 7) ÷ 44

⇒ r = 3 × 7

⇒ r = 21 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 21 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Remolding 2D Shapes

When a wire is bent or reshaped from one 2D figure to another, its total length or boundary perimeter always remains constant.

Area and Perimeter Relation

For a given constant perimeter, a circle always encloses the maximum possible area compared to any other 2D polygon like a square, rectangle or triangle.

Remolding 3D Shapes

Similar to 2D figures, when a solid 3D object is melted and recast into another shape, its total volume remains strictly constant.

questions.question: The ratio of the outer and the inner circumferences of a circular path is 11 ∶ 7. If path is 20 metres wide, then what is the radius of the inner circle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of circumferences of two circles is identical to the ratio of their radii.

⇒ Outer Radius (R) : Inner Radius (r) = 11 : 7

⇒ Difference in ratio parts = 11 − 7 = 4 parts

⇒ This difference corresponds to the path width: 4 parts = 20 m ⇒ 1 part = 5 m

⇒ Inner radius (r) = 7 parts = 7 × 5 = 35 m

**∴ The correct answer is 35 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of outer circumference to inner circumference = 11 : 7

Width of the circular path = 20 metres

**Formula Used:**

Circumference of a circle = 2 × π × Radius

Width of circular path = Outer Radius (R) − Inner Radius (r)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f845fecabe9b7af088360320fdc979676f90fdc522c37d0665abb88aa9734b9a.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the outer radius be R and the inner radius be r.

⇒ (2 × π × R) / (2 × π × r) = 11 / 7

⇒ R / r = 11 / 7

⇒ Let R = 11x and r = 7x

⇒ Width of path = R − r = 20

⇒ 11x − 7x = 20

⇒ 4x = 20

⇒ x = 5

⇒ Inner radius (r) = 7x = 7 × 5 = 35 metres.

**∴ The correct answer is 35 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Circular Path

The area of the track between two concentric circles can be calculated using the formula Area = π × (R² − r²), where R is the outer radius and r is the inner radius.

Circumference and Radius Relationship

The ratio of the circumferences of any two circles is always exactly equal to the ratio of their respective radii or diameters (C₁ / C₂ = r₁ / r₂).

Area and Radius Relationship

The ratio of the areas of two circles is equal to the square of the ratio of their radii (A₁ / A₂ = (r₁ / r₂)²).
</p

questions.question: In a village, there is a pond that has the radius 14 m. There is a fountain of diameter 14 m in the centre of the pond. Calculate the area of the pond excluding the fountain. ( { Use } pi=(22)/(7))
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The radius of the pond is 14 m.

The diameter of the fountain is 14 m, so its radius is 7 m.

**Formula Used:**

Area of a circle = π × r²

Area of the pond excluding the fountain = Area of the pond - Area of the fountain

**Calculation:**

**Step 1:** Calculate the area of the pond:

Area of the pond = π × (14)²

⇒ Area of the pond = (22/7) × 196 = 616 m²

**Step 2:** Calculate the area of the fountain:

Area of the fountain = π × (7)²

⇒ Area of the fountain = (22/7) × 49 = 154 m²

**Step 3:** Subtract the area of the fountain from the area of the pond:

A circle is inscribed in an equilateral triangle of side 30 cm.

where a = side of the triangle

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3f0d4e9feef433f07f77afce55279bd29c6af671204d3337b3b6436ae287af69.png] **

Let the triangle be Δ ABC with sides, a = 30 cm,

and draw the angle bisectors of all three angles of the triangle as shown in the above figure.

Let the centre of the circle be O. 

Here, OP = OQ = OR = r where r = radius of the circle

We have O as the incentre and OP, OQ and OR are equal.

 Now, from the above figure,

Area of Δ ABC = Area of Δ OAB + Area of Δ OBC + Area of Δ OCA

⇒ √3/4 × a² = (1/2 × AB × OP) + (1/2 × BC × OR) + (1/2 × AC × OQ)

⇒ √3/4 × (30)² = (1/2 × a × r) + (1/2 × a × r) + (1/2 × a × r)

⇒ √3/4 × 900 = 3 × (1/2 × 30 × r)

⇒ r = 15/√3 cm

⇒ Area of the Circle = π × (15/√3)²

So, AO ∶ OR = 2 ∶ 1

⇒ OR ∶ AR = 1 ∶ 3 

So, from the above figure, Radius of Circle, r = OR 

⇒ r = (1/3) × AR

⇒ r = (1/3) × 15√3

⇒ r = 15/√3 cm

Now, Area of the Circle = πr2

⇒ Area of the Circle = π × (15/√3)2

∴ The area of the triangle is 75π cm2

questions.question: A 70 cm wide path is made around a circular garden having a diameter of 14 metres. What is the area of the path (in m²)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of a circular path of width w outside a circle of radius r is given by π × w × (2r + w).

Given width w = 70 cm = 0.7 m and inner radius r = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 m.

⇒ Area = π × 0.7 × (2 × 7 + 0.7)

⇒ Area = π × 0.7 × 14.7 = 10.29 π

**∴ The correct answer is 10.29 π m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of the circular garden = 14 m

Width of the path (w) = 70 cm = 0.7 m

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/73cdcdbcc521b0b75a4f1424617c35b253d93615e7ede3ef40474ca30c758703.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Area of circular ring = π × (R² − r²)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Radius of the inner garden (r) = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 m

⇒ Radius of the outer circle (R) = 7 + 0.7 = 7.7 m

⇒ Area of the path = π × (7.7² − 7²)

⇒ Area of the path = π × (7.7 − 7) × (7.7 + 7)

⇒ Area of the path = π × 0.7 × 14.7

⇒ Area of the path = 10.29 π m²

**∴ The correct answer is 10.29 π m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Circular Ring

The area enclosed between two concentric circles of radii R and r (where R > r) is given by π(R² − r²).

Path Inside a Circle

If a path of width w is constructed inside a circular garden of radius R, the area of the path becomes π × w × (2R − w).

Length of Arc and Area of Sector

For a circle of radius r, length of an arc subtending angle θ is (θ÷360) × 2πr, and the area of the sector is (θ÷360) × πr².
